key_insight: Clinical and demographic data from TB screening patients in Uganda and South Africa can support machine-learning models that help decide who should receive costly molecular testing.
clinical_relevance: A simple logistic regression model with feature selection performed strongly across held-out country cohorts, suggesting practical cross-site TB triage potential.
method: Used the CAGE-TB dataset from presumptive TB patients in South Africa and Uganda.
Compared logistic regression, multilayer perceptrons, and convolutional neural networks.
Applied greedy feature selection; for CNNs, feature selection and ordering were jointly optimized.
evidence_signal: Feature selection improved development AUROC by 2–7%, and logistic regression achieved AUROC 0.80 on Uganda and 0.84 on South Africa in held-out testing.
watch_item: Deeper neural networks did not generalize consistently across countries, and the best model still fell short of WHO minimum sensitivity targets by 4–9%.
paper_title: Cross-cohort TB classification using clinical data gathered in Uganda and South Africa
